variants.headline: Looking back: builder left unpaid for work done
variants.sub: The builder {builder} is owed payment by the client {client} for completed work.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: The client {client} had not paid {builder} for building work done.

Work done is work that deserves a serious account of payment. Labour should keep that connection visible without making an employer's receipt the whole measure of a worker's life. A missed obligation is a proper subject of scrutiny, not something to disappear behind a tidy description of construction progress.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The conduct of {target} merits scrutiny against the unpaid work. This account records the amount owed and the stopping rule without presuming that the current failure has already reached that rule's threshold.
